title: Revise defaults-loop design: apply review 1, add introspection step
summary: Edit docs/design/defaults-loop.md to make all seven changes in review 1 (F1 to F5, the two Medium items, the Low items), and add introspection as a first-class step whose records feed the loop. Design only: no code, and no edits to BRIEF.md, defaults.toml or the review.

defaults_applied.how: The change is itself a design revision with alternatives (gateway fallback vs explicit second call; assignment vs pairwise clustering) written down.
Each case (8qkc, m1bs, 69gf, t1y6, 3p3y, jk8v, 16zf, #47) is cited with a source and labelled reported or measured; numbers are labelled estimates.
One document revision with the minimal decision/changelog follow-ups; no code.
Written for an outside reader with route and shapes spelled out.
Introspection step asks for the cause beyond the instance; the revision fixes review root causes (F1, F2) rather than patching wording.
Each prevention in the design is marked as a default, a code check, or a design change; prose-only rules are marked as such.
No secrets or personal data in the document.
Design reviewed against the review's checklist by an independent verifier.

assumptions: The BRIEF.md addendum '2026-10-13: Introspection on every correction' is summarised in the request; the producer should read it in the repository if present and not edit it.

'Make every change listed' means the seven items in section 5 of the review, including the Low items (D26 'eleven', RM-3 citation, measure render()) so far as they can be done without code; the render() measurement is written as a gate for the build job, since this is design only.
D90 in docs/decisions.md must be updated to match the revised design (review item 1), and D26 text corrected, so decisions.md is modified.
docs/design/roadmap.md RM-3 citation is corrected where the design or roadmap cites it; the roadmap is changed only if it holds the faulty citation.
Today's operator-found cases are cited by job id as the operator reported them (user-reported); records/ is absent, so counts are labelled reported, not measured.
Introspection records are a new typed record schema described in prose only; no change to docs/records.md unless a pointer is needed, and no Rust code.
CHANGELOG.md gets an entry in the repository's usual style, per D89.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults-loop.md restates the Jev steps so Jev only answers typed questions (assignment of a record to a cluster, or pairwise boolean), and a language model drafts the statement, applies_to and title; D90 in docs/decisions.md matches (F1).

Section 2 labels the R2 reader-budget overrun as a counter-example (a repeat that belongs in code, used as a 'none' label), states R1 is closed in code by D89, marks the case for the loop as unproved, and makes 'at least N distinct jobs that a default would cover' a gate before any build (F2).

A section names POST /v1/evaluate, the request fields (model, state, questions with type, instructions, criteria), the response fields (choice, probabilities, confidence), the chat-route refusal as a build error not a retry, and says the fake Jev follows that shape and cost/tokens are read from the response (F4).
The design defines the top-probability and confidence signals, what each controls, chooses between gateway fallback and an explicit second call, and stores the answering model in evidence (F5).

The reader budget is stated in terms of the first sentence plus id/scope and entry count, says where the full statement lands, defines the intervention record as the single counted unit (a correction not counted twice, answer-kind corrections handled), and the render() measurement with the live counter is a gate on the 1,500-token estimate.

The promotion criterion computes the test-part size needed for a skill lower bound, or the interval is dropped in favour of a user judgment (F3); D26 'eleven' is corrected and the RM-3 citation fixed.

Introspection is a first-class step in the loop: every correction, intervention, rejection and failure triggers one that Athena runs and records itself, with fields for what happened, failure class and earlier cases of the class, cause beyond the instance, prevention (default, code check, or design change), and a proposed next request; a retry starts from the record; the defaults loop consumes the records; matching a case to a class is a typed decision through /v1/evaluate.

The document uses the operator's cases as evidence, each labelled reported: CHANGELOG exclusion (8qkc, m1bs); reader budget failing four jobs (69gf, t1y6, 3p3y, jk8v) with retries patching only the last finding; 'checks not finished' on #47 with no hung-CI diagnosis; Haiku untested work (69gf); plan to edit owner-only BRIEF.md (16zf); plans bundling design and build; Jev's interface assumed not checked. For each it states the class and what would have prevented it.
No Rust, config, defaults.toml, BRIEF.md, records/ or review file is changed; CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
Run `git status` and `git diff --stat`: only markdown files under docs/ and CHANGELOG.md are changed, and cargo test still passes with no source changes.

out_of_scope: Any Rust code, Jev client, fake, or introspection implementation
Editing BRIEF.md, defaults.toml, records/ or the review file
Calling the gateway or measuring render() live
Adding defaults entries or a changelog default
Reading the records to verify the x4 counts
departures: Higher cost and time and lower verification than the reference: a long design doc rewrite with many checklist items, two combined asks, and decisions.md edits; the verifier has many content criteria to satisfy.
